scholarships.title: Boren Scholarships and Fellowships (National Security Education Program)
scholarships.official_source: Defense Language and National Security Education Office (DLNSEO), National Security Education Program

existing.funding_period: maximum award determined by duration abroad
existing.description: The National Security Education Program awards Boren Scholarships and Fellowships to U.S. undergraduate and graduate students committed to long-term overseas study and to federal service. Boren Scholarships fund study abroad by U.S. undergraduates and Boren Fellowships fund research and language study proposals by U.S. graduate students, in world regions critical to U.S. interests. Maximum awards are determined by duration abroad: $25,000 for 25-52 weeks (preferred), $12,500 for 12-24 weeks, and $8,000 for 8-11 weeks for STEM majors under the Scholarships programme. There are no minimum language requirements except French and Spanish, which require intermediate high [1+] proficiency for advanced study programs in Africa and Latin America. The Boren Awards are an initiative of the Defense Language and National Security Education Office.
eligibility: Be a U.S. undergraduate (Boren Scholarship) or graduate student (Boren Fellowship)
Commit to long-term overseas study in a world region critical to U.S. interests
Pursue a career with the federal government and accept the one-year federal service requirement
For Boren Scholarships studying STEM, satisfy the additional criteria for the shorter 8-11 week award tier
existing.eligibility_summary: U.S. undergraduate and graduate students committed to long-term overseas study in world regions critical to U.S. interests, who intend to pursue a career and long-term service in the federal government.
benefits: $8,000 for 8-11 weeks abroad, available to STEM majors only under the Boren Scholarships
Access to the Boren Awards campus representative network and alumni community
coverage: Overseas study or research programme costs up to the tier maximum set by duration abroad
Language study and area studies in regions critical to U.S. interests
requirements: Study or research abroad in a region critical to U.S. interests
Accept the one-year federal service requirement
Submit by the national deadline; campus representatives may set earlier campus deadlines that must also be respected
There are no minimum language requirements except French and Spanish, which require intermediate high [1+] proficiency for advanced study programs in Africa and Latin America
documents: Completed online application created through the Apply Now page, selecting overseas location and language
Application essays, drafted as early as possible and shared with recommenders
Recommendation materials from the referees named in the application
Any supporting programme and language documentation required by the selected programme
existing.english_requirement: There are no minimum language requirements, with the exception of French and Spanish, which require intermediate high [1+] proficiency for advanced study programs in Africa and Latin America.
application_method: Visit the Apply Now page and create a new application, selecting the overseas location and language to be studied
Contact the Boren Awards campus representative at your institution for advice (you may still apply if your institution has none)
Watch the official introductory webinar and review the official selection criteria
Choose a Regional Flagship Language Initiative programme or design your own study programme
Draft essays early and share them with recommenders
Submit by the national deadline, and by any campus deadline your representative sets
existing.selection_notes: The homepage directs applicants to review the official selection criteria, and frames professional goals as critical: the Boren Awards invest in linguistic and cultural knowledge for aspiring federal government employees, so the national security implications of the study and career opportunities matter to a successful application.
existing.best_fit: U.S. students at any degree level who can commit to a federal career and a one-year federal service obligation, and who want funded overseas study or research in a world region critical to U.S. interests.
existing.notes: 2027-28 funding may be applied to programs starting as early as June 2027 or as late as March 1, 2028. The Regional Flagship Language Initiative offers credit-bearing language courses in summer domestically and fall overseas for the African Flagship Languages Initiative (French, Swahili, Akan/Twi, Wolof or Zulu), with the option to continue overseas study into the spring.
existing.application_period: Annual cycle tied to the academic year. 2027-28 funding may be applied to programs starting as early as June 2027 or as late as March 1, 2028.
existing.deadline_display: National deadlines for the 2027 Boren Awards: Boren Fellowships January 20, 2027; Boren Scholarships January 27, 2027. 2027-28 Boren Awards funding may be applied to programs starting as early as June 2027 or as late as March 1, 2028. Applicants are notified of selection in mid-to-late April.
existing.program_type: Federal overseas study and research scholarship for U.S. students in national security critical regions

scholarships.title: OAS-AUWCL Scholarship Program (American University Washington College of Law LL.M.)
scholarships.official_source: Organization of American States, General Secretariat (with American University Washington College of Law)

existing.description: The OAS-AUWCL Scholarship Program awards a 50% tuition waiver for the LL.M. programmes of American University Washington College of Law in Washington, D.C., under the OAS Partnerships Program for Education and Training (PAEC). It is open to citizens and permanent legal residents of any active OAS member state other than the United States who hold a JD from an ABA-accredited US law school or an equivalent foreign law degree and are admitted to an AUWCL LL.M. programme. Applicants apply for admission through AUWCL, which then issues the Admissions Letter used for scholarship consideration; the Spring 2027 deadlines are 1 November 2026 for residential study and 30 November 2026 for hybrid and online study. The award covers 50% of published tuition; recipients pay the remaining tuition, mandatory fees, health insurance, books, graduation and visa costs, travel, and all other living and study costs, and must commit to return to work in their sponsoring country for the duration of the scholarship.
eligibility: Be admitted to one of the LL.M. programmes offered by American University Washington College of Law
Be a citizen and/or permanent legal resident of any active OAS member state, except the United States
Hold a Juris Doctor (JD) from a US law school accredited by the American Bar Association, or a first degree in law from a foreign law school with equivalent standards
Not be a current OAS scholarship recipient
Applicants from Argentina must complete the required form and send it to the National Liaison Office (ONE) in Argentina
International applicants must meet AUWCL's English Language Proficiency Requirement (English programmes only); the Spanish-language programme does not require English proficiency
existing.eligibility_summary: Citizens and/or permanent legal residents of any active OAS member state except the United States, who hold a Juris Doctor from an ABA-accredited US law school or a first law degree from a foreign law school of equivalent standard, and who are admitted to one of the AUWCL LL.M. programmes. Open to new applicants and to current AUWCL students; not open to current OAS scholarship holders, GS/OAS staff, consultants, Permanent Officials or their immediate relatives.
benefits: 50% tuition waiver at American University Washington College of Law, applied by AUWCL on admission
Scholarship benefits are subject to the academic performance of the recipient and to the availability of funds
coverage: 50% of the LL.M. tuition fee (USD 30,972 of the USD 61,944 published total tuition)
requirements: Submit a completed application through AUWCL's website with supporting documents before the application deadline
Once admitted, AUWCL issues an Admissions Letter to be considered for the scholarship
Sign the OAS/AUWCL Acceptance Form accepting the scholarship and its terms and conditions
Maintain a GPA of at least 3.0/4.0 to retain the scholarship
Selections are published in August and December at www.oas.org/scholarships
documents: Supporting documents requested by AUWCL for admission
existing.english_requirement: English language proficiency required for the English-language LL.M. programmes (AUWCL English Language Proficiency Requirement); the LL.M. en Derechos Humanos y Derecho Humanitario is taught in Spanish and does not require English proficiency
application_method: Apply for admission to the AUWCL LL.M. programme online at https://www.american.edu/wcl/academics/degrees/llm/how-to-apply/online.cfm
On admission, AUWCL issues an Admissions Letter for the scholarship consideration
Selected awardees sign the OAS/AUWCL Acceptance Form
existing.selection_notes: AUWCL and the OAS select awardees on the merits and overall credentials of the candidate (academic and professional background), geographical distribution of applicants taking into account the greater needs of smaller and relatively less developed economies, the potential for impact of the applicant's essay upon return to their country of origin, and gender diversity.
existing.best_fit: Graduates of a law school in an OAS member state other than the United States who need an American LL.M. in international human rights, humanitarian law or international arbitration and business law, and who can fund the remaining 50% of tuition plus fees, insurance, books, travel and living costs.
existing.notes:
The OAS Rowe Fund educational loan programme (interest-free loans of up to USD 15,000 for Latin American and Caribbean citizens studying at accredited US universities) is mentioned in the announcement as a separate route for applicants who cannot cover the balance; it is not part of this award.
Funding period: for the degree programme (50% of the published total tuition of USD 61,944; 2026-2027 academic credit price USD 2,581)
existing.duration: 2-3 semesters (LL.M. in International Human Rights and Humanitarian Law); 2-10 semesters (LL.M. en Derechos Humanos y Derecho Humanitario); 9-18 months (LL.M. in International Arbitration and Business Law)
existing.application_period: Spring 2027 intake: admission through AUWCL and scholarship application deadlines of 1 November 2026 (residential) and 30 November 2026 (hybrid/online); classes begin January 2027
existing.deadline_display: 1 November 2026 (residential/in-person LL.M., Spring 2027); 30 November 2026 (hybrid and online LL.M., Spring 2027)
existing.program_type: Regional intergovernmental scholarship programme (OAS Partnerships Program for Education and Training, PAEC)
